page.a11y.title: Accessibility statement
page.a11y.description: The Battle for Middle-earth website aims to comply with WCAG 2.1 AA. What we have done, where the limits are, and how to report a problem.
page.a11y.subtitle: What we’ve done, where the boundaries are, and how to get in touch when something doesn’t work.
page.a11y.intro_p1_post: as the operator of www.panprstenu.cz commits to ensuring the accessibility of its websites in accordance with Czech Act No. 99/2019 Coll. on the accessibility of websites and mobile applications, which implements Directive (EU) 2016/2102 of the European Parliament and of the Council.
page.a11y.intro_p2: This accessibility statement applies to www.panprstenu.cz and all its subpages.
page.a11y.compliance_p: The website aims to comply with WCAG 2.1 level AA and takes into account the recommendations of EN 301 549. Some content may, in certain contexts, require minor adjustments — we address these continuously.
page.a11y.compliance_l1: Skip-to-content link to the main content (Tab from URL).
page.a11y.compliance_l2: Semantic HTML structure with landmarks (header, nav, main, footer).
page.a11y.compliance_l3: Keyboard operability of all interactive elements (Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, Esc).
page.a11y.compliance_l4: Visible focus ring in a prominent gold colour.
page.a11y.compliance_l5: Text contrast ≥ 4.5:1 for normal text, ≥ 3:1 for large text.
page.a11y.compliance_l6: Rules and organisational accordions use native <details> — they work without JavaScript and with screen readers.
page.a11y.compliance_l7_intro: Floating accessibility panel (bottom right) — the user can:
page.a11y.compliance_l7_c: switch to a sans-serif font (suitable for dyslexia),
page.a11y.compliance_l8: Respect for system preferences prefers-reduced-motion and prefers-color-scheme.
page.a11y.compliance_l9: Meaningful image text and alternative descriptions where needed.
page.a11y.compliance_l10: Hreflang for 5 language versions (cs, en, de, sk, uk).
page.a11y.compliance_l12: Style consistency and support for 100% browser zoom (Ctrl/Cmd +).
page.a11y.lim_p: Some parts of the website may, in individual cases, show minor deviations from WCAG 2.1 AA. Specifically:
page.a11y.lim_l1_pre: The embedded Google Maps in the section
page.a11y.lim_l1_post: is a third party and its accessibility is managed by Google. The event location is also given separately as plain text (GPS coordinates + link).
page.a11y.lim_l2: Decorative images (corner ornaments, wax seals, dividers) have aria-hidden="true" — they are hidden from screen readers so as not to clutter the listening experience.
page.a11y.lim_l3: The photo gallery from past editions does not yet have automatic alternative text for every shot — this will be added by the MVP launch.
page.a11y.prep_p1: This statement was prepared on 30 April 2026 based on a self-assessment carried out directly by the operator (tested by keyboard, screen reader, automated tools and manual contrast checks).
page.a11y.prep_p2: The statement was last reviewed on 30 April 2026.

page.helpers.title: Helpers
page.helpers.subtitle: Without you the camp wouldn’t stand. Without us, neither.
page.helpers.who_p1: Helpers are participants who want to help with organisation, preparation, the programme or camp logistics. You can help short-term, for the whole weekend, or only during a specific phase of the event.
page.helpers.who_p2_pre: At the same time, a helper does not have to miss out on the experience. Help happens
page.helpers.who_p2_post: and can be set up so that you can still enjoy The Lord of the Rings as a regular participant.
page.helpers.who_p3: A helper might be someone who:
page.helpers.who_l1: is coming to the event for the first time and wants to get involved,
page.helpers.who_l2: doesn’t want to fight but wants to be useful,
page.helpers.who_l3: wants to play normally and also help with a specific part of the programme,
page.helpers.who_l5: wants to support their army or the whole camp,
page.helpers.who_l6: wants to get close to the organising team and gradually do more.
page.helpers.h_60s: The most important things in 60 seconds
page.helpers.s60_l1: A helper is not automatically an organiser.
page.helpers.s60_l2: You only help according to what was agreed, your time and your possibilities.
page.helpers.s60_l3: You can still enjoy the event as a regular participant.
page.helpers.s60_l4: You can help with registration, the programme, logistics, the children’s game, clean-up or camp logistics.
page.helpers.s60_l5: If you commit to something, we count on you.
page.helpers.s60_l6: Depending on how much you contribute, we may reward you with a discount, a fee waiver or covered food and drink.
page.helpers.s60_l7: If you’re not sure, ask first rather than improvising in a sensitive situation.
page.helpers.what1_p: Helping with checking in participants, paperwork, parking cards and orientation for new arrivals. Suitable for patient people who can communicate well and keep order even when many people arrive at once.
page.helpers.what2_p: Helping with the programme for young adventurers. Suitable for people who like children, are patient and can keep an eye on safety as well as atmosphere. May involve activity stations, games, crafts, side activities or simple logistics.
page.helpers.what3_p: Helping with arenas, the market, micro-quests, capture-the-flag, small games or side programme. Friday is the perfect space for camp life and smaller in-game activities.
page.helpers.what4_p: Helping with water, firewood, small repairs, waste, orientation for visitors, area checks, signage or coordination with the pub. These aren’t the most visible roles, but often the most important.
page.helpers.what5_p: Helping with line-up, instructions, movement, organising space or playing NPCs. During the main game it is essential to follow the instructions of responsible organisers and not to improvise where it could affect safety or the course of play.
page.helpers.what6_p: Packing, cleaning the campsite, checking the area after the event and helping leave the place tidy. Sunday is not the in-game finale — it’s the day we clean up after ourselves and say goodbye.

page.hobbits.full1_p1: Hobbits are not naturally a battle people. That is what makes them so interesting in play. Their strength is not in heavy armour, big shields and a thunderous charge, but in togetherness, courage out of necessity, supplies, news, light movement, common sense and the ability to survive even where larger nations find their pride too cramped.
page.hobbits.full1_p2: For game purposes hobbits can be approached as a supporting, light and community-minded army of the Free Peoples. They can be messengers, cooks, quartermasters, scouts, water-bearers, careful archers, keepers of camp comfort, gatherers of news and small fighters who got into the battle mostly because someone had to hold the last way home.
page.hobbits.full1_p3: A hobbit costume should look different from a human one at first sight. You don’t need to be physically small. What matters are proportions, layering, softness, country cut, colour, roundness and small civilian details: vest, shirt, breeches, braces, pockets, mug, unlit pipe, snack, map, lantern, tobacco pouch or a dried apple.
page.hobbits.full2_p1: Hobbits are a small folk related to humans, known above all from the Shire, Rhovanion and around Bree. They tend to be smaller, with hairy feet that have hard skin, often walking barefoot, and curly hair. They aren’t a great historical nation of kings and wars, yet their unobtrusiveness has proven an unexpected strength in Middle-earth’s history.
page.hobbits.full2_p2: Most hobbits prefer food, gardens, crafts, inns, songs, birthdays, gift-giving and a comfortable home over adventure. That doesn’t mean they are cowards. They are cautious, practical, and slow to believe that the great events of history really concern their fields and pantries.
page.hobbits.full2_p3: For play purposes you can distinguish hobbits from the quieter Shire, the bolder Brandybucks and Tooks, the more water-loving Stoors and the more practical hobbits from Bree. You don’t have to copy the exact family lineage. It’s enough that the costume and behaviour show a small country folk who view war with mistrust but won’t let their friends down.
page.hobbits.full3_p1: Hobbit clothing is based on comfortable country wear. Linen or cotton shirts, wool vests, knee breeches, braces, wide belts, colourful scarves, soft jackets, capes, hoods and simple caps all fit. Colours can be earthy, but hobbits can carry more colour than soldiers: green, brown, beige, yellow, burgundy, dark blue and muted red.
page.hobbits.full3_p2: The most important thing is not to look modern. A T-shirt, hoodie, sports trousers and trainers without cover destroy a hobbit instantly. Modern boots can be hidden under foot covers, leg wraps or fur covers to give the impression of hobbit feet. Walking barefoot in the terrain is not recommended for safety reasons.
page.hobbits.full3_p3: Small props belong to a hobbit. A wooden spoon, mug, napkin, small pan, basket, food pouch, lantern, recipe book, map, letter, ball of string or a small spade do more than re-equipping into heavy armour. A hobbit should look like they originally went out to run an errand and somebody dragged them into history by mistake.
page.hobbits.full4_p1: A hobbit is, above all, not a heavy infantryman. If they fight, a short sword, a dagger according to the rules, a staff, a small round shield, a sling-stylisation per rules, a light bow or a simple spear all suit. Equipment should be small, practical and rather defensive. Heavy two-handed weapons and large metal armour usually don’t fit a hobbit.
page.hobbits.full4_p2: A camp-support role works very well. Hobbits can help with water, food, small tasks, messages, escorting newcomers, trade, coins, watches and the in-camp atmosphere. If they take part in battle, they can hold the second line, protect the banner, escort the wounded, carry messages or support the bigger fighters.
page.hobbits.full4_p3: A hobbit group should play on togetherness. An individual can be comic, but a group of hobbits should be a small island of home in the middle of war. A shared breakfast, regular snacks, “fundamental” debates about pies and a calm resistance to grand speeches can be a very strong part of the atmosphere.
page.hobbits.full5_p1: Hobbits don’t usually come to the event to win the contest for the most fearsome look. Their tone is friendly, nosy, a little careful and a little cheeky. They might ask why everyone looks so serious, whether lunch is coming yet and whether it’s really necessary to go to battle right now.
page.hobbits.full5_p2: A nice contrast works well: a hobbit is afraid, but goes anyway. Doesn’t want to be a hero, but does the right thing. Doesn’t want to leave camp, but if a friend goes, goes with them. Doesn’t know grand strategy, but knows exactly where the water is, who has the last bandage and who lost their mug.
page.hobbits.full5_p3: For newcomers, a hobbit is a very pleasant role. The costume can start simple and grow. You don’t need expensive armour. The key is a comfortable country look, modern items covered up, and the willingness to play small situations with others.
page.hobbits.full6_l1: A shirt, vest, breeches, braces and a cloak make a base in one evening.
page.hobbits.full6_l2: Use earthy and gently cheerful colours: green, brown, beige, yellow, burgundy.
page.hobbits.full6_l3: Cover modern boots with foot covers, fur or leg wraps. Don’t walk barefoot in dangerous terrain.
page.hobbits.full6_l4: Add civilian props: mug, spoon, basket, map, lantern, snack.
page.hobbits.full6_l5: Keep weapons small and practical. A hobbit should look clever, not like a knight at half size.
page.hobbits.full6_l6: In a group, agree on a family or village element: scarves, buttons, a patch, vest colour or a round-door symbol.

page.kids.h_who: Who is the children’s game for?
page.kids.who_p1: The children’s game is for children who are still too young for the main battle but want to enjoy their own adventure, games, crafts, stations and the atmosphere of Middle-earth.
page.kids.who_p2_pre: The main battle and event participation is from

page.kids.age_note: We are not a kindergarten or babysitting service — we want to give children an adventure, but safety and well-being always come first.
page.kids.h_60s: The most important things in 60 seconds
page.kids.s60_l1: The main game and battle is age 12+.
page.kids.s60_l2: For younger children we run a separate children’s game.

page.kids.s60_l5: The programme runs mainly on Friday and on Saturday during the main game.
page.kids.s60_l6: On Saturday we run stations, tasks and the kids’ own adventure.
page.kids.s60_l7: We ask parents for cooperation, help and a realistic assessment of their child’s abilities.
page.kids.s60_l8: Parental involvement is welcome and very much appreciated.

page.kids.p1_desc: If you arrive with children already on Thursday, we plan from about 16:00 onwards a lighter introductory programme — a team game, movement activities or a more relaxed programme depending on the situation.
page.kids.p2_desc: Sports games, low rope obstacles, drawing and crafts, archery-style shooting, throwing at targets, forest activities, a jewellery-making workshop and other small games and stations.
page.kids.p3_desc: A short atmospheric path of courage ending with a scene with elves. We adjust it to the age and courage of the children.
page.kids.p4_desc: Tasks, physical activities, riddles, puzzles, throwing, treasure hunting and small story elements. Includes a snack or “lunch from the hobbit pantry”.
page.kids.p5_desc: After returning to the meadow, a more relaxed programme, crafts or further activities until the armies return from the main game.
page.kids.program_alert_pre: The programme may change based on the weather, the number of children, ages and conditions on site.
page.kids.program_alert_strong: Children’s safety and well-being take precedence over an exact schedule.
page.kids.what_p1: The children’s game is meant to be playful, safe and atmospheric. It isn’t a small copy of the main battle. Children don’t need to fight like adult players. We want to offer them their own adventure where they can be small hobbits, elves, dwarves, messengers, treasure hunters or brave wanderers.
page.kids.parents_p1: Parents are important for the children’s game. We will be glad if you:

page.kids.parents_l2: explain to them what awaits them,
page.kids.parents_l3: remain available if we need you,
page.kids.parents_l5: join in the programme if it appeals to you.
page.kids.parents_p2: For younger children, parental participation is necessary. For older children it depends on their independence, courage and an arrangement on site.
page.kids.parents_p3: We very much appreciate parental involvement. The more good adult hands we have, the nicer and safer an adventure we can build for the children.

page.camp_life.meta_title: Camp life — coins, quests, Friday programme and life in camp
page.camp_life.description: The Lord of the Rings 2026 is not only the Saturday battle. Come already on Thursday or Friday and live camp life in Middle-earth: coins, trade, small quests, the Friday game, faction camp and a programme for young adventurers.
page.camp_life.title: Camp life
page.camp_life.subtitle: Come earlier. Middle-earth begins in the camp.
page.camp_life.intro_p1: The Lord of the Rings isn’t just the Saturday battle. We want the campsite to turn into a piece of Middle-earth from the moment you arrive — with its own atmosphere, armies, fires, trade, song, small games, services, quests and encounters. For 2026 we’re preparing several new things to support play outside the main battle.
page.camp_life.h_60s: The most important things in 60 seconds
page.camp_life.s60_l1: Each participant gets a number of in-game coins at registration.
page.camp_life.s60_l2: Coins can be used for small games, bets, services, trade and atmospheric play in camp.
page.camp_life.s60_l3: We want the campsite to be more divided by armies and sides.
page.camp_life.s60_l4: Friday will be devoted to play in camp, the side programme, arenas, capture-the-flag and the children’s game.
page.camp_life.s60_l5: Micro personal quests and small tasks will appear.
page.camp_life.s60_l6_pre: For children we’re preparing a separate
page.camp_life.s60_l7_strong: None of this will work without you.
page.camp_life.s60_l7_post: Camp life only happens if you actually want to play.
page.camp_life.news1_desc: Games, bets, services, trade. Coins bring camp life alive.
page.camp_life.news2_desc: A dividing line between the light and dark sides. Armies together.
page.camp_life.news3_desc: A team game in camp. Shorter format, suitable for newcomers too.
page.camp_life.news4_desc: Trade, bards, mercenaries, fortune-tellers. The best things will come from you.
page.camp_life.news5_desc: Small tasks: deliver a message, win a bet, find a person.
page.camp_life.news6_desc: A separate programme for children aged 5–9. Their own adventure.
page.camp_life.mince_p1: Each participant will receive a number of in-game coins at the start of the event. We are preparing several types of coins so they fit different peoples and races of Middle-earth.
page.camp_life.mince_p2: By default we count on a simple 1:1 rate between the coin types. But Middle-earth isn’t an accountant’s spreadsheet. It will be up to you whether you keep this rate or start creating your own value, agreements and trading customs among yourselves.
page.camp_life.mince_use_intro: Coins are mainly meant to support camp life. You can use them for example:
page.camp_life.mince_l3: for bets on arenas and tournaments,
page.camp_life.mince_use_note: Want firewood for the fire? Hire someone to help. Want bards by your fire? Even bards don’t live on glory alone. Want to try archery in the elven camp? It might cost something. Want to order a night watch? Mercenaries also have their worldly needs.
page.camp_life.mince_pub_p_pre: We also count on the option of using coins as a game element in arrangement with the
page.camp_life.mince_pub_p_post: . We’ll specify the exact conditions and scope of use later.
page.camp_life.mince_alert_title: Coins are not an official currency
page.camp_life.mince_alert_strong: are not normal money or a claimable discount
page.camp_life.mince_alert_post: . They are game items meant to enliven camp life. Their use at the inn, with organisers or in specific activities will be governed by the agreement and rules of the event.
page.camp_life.mince_h_more: How do I get more coins
page.camp_life.mince_more_intro: Each participant gets the basic number of coins on registration on site. You can earn more for example:
page.camp_life.mince_more_l2: by taking part in arenas, tournaments and games,
page.camp_life.mince_more_l3: by offering services to other players,
page.camp_life.mince_more_l5: by helping the organisers with preparation,
page.camp_life.mince_more_l6: through your own creativity and engagement in camp life.
page.camp_life.tab_p1: In recent years the campsite has changed substantially. Historical tents, themed shelters and period camps have multiplied so much that they are no longer just a small extra somewhere on the edge of the meadow.
page.camp_life.tab_p2: At the same time we keep hearing from groups, lords and commanders that they want to be together with their army. They want a shared fire, to talk things over, play camp life, drill and create the atmosphere of their side.
page.camp_life.tab_p3_pre: That’s why we want to divide the campsite for 2026 more by armies and sides. The dividing path / line will naturally run between the
page.camp_life.tab_l1: Armies and groups should have a better chance to camp together.
page.camp_life.tab_l2: The camp will turn more into a play space.
page.camp_life.tab_l3: It will be easier to play faction life.
page.camp_life.tab_l4: Period and themed tents will still be welcome.
page.camp_life.tab_l5: We recommend masking modern tents as much as possible with tarps, fabric or non-distracting placement.
page.camp_life.tab_l6: If you can buy or borrow a historical tent, it will help the atmosphere a lot.
page.camp_life.tab_alert: This year we want to see the camp as part of the game. It’s not just where you sleep. It’s about creating the feeling of an army camp in Middle-earth from the moment of arrival.
page.camp_life.vl_p1: Friday won’t just be waiting for the Saturday battle. We want there to be play already on Friday.
page.camp_life.vl_p2: We are preparing a Friday game in camp, including capture-the-flag and other side activities. The goal isn’t to create a second main battle — the goal is to get the camp moving, involve the armies, support the atmosphere and give participants a reason to arrive earlier.
page.camp_life.vl_l1: a simple team game in or around the camp,
page.camp_life.vl_l4: a shorter format than the Saturday battle,
page.camp_life.vl_l5: emphasis on movement, cooperation and atmosphere,
page.camp_life.vl_l6: no need to know the whole Saturday scenario.
page.camp_life.vl_note: Exact rules, times and the way to take part will be added during June.
page.camp_life.z_p1: Camp life isn’t just organiser-run activities. The best things often happen between participants.
page.camp_life.z_intro: We want to support you to:
page.camp_life.z_l8: play your character outside the battlefield too.
page.camp_life.z_i1: a dwarven tap by the fire,
page.camp_life.z_i11: a scribe of contracts and bets.
page.camp_life.z_box_title: I want to take part but don’t know how
page.camp_life.z_box_l5: join in a game or arena,
page.camp_life.z_box_l7: don’t be afraid to start with something small.
page.camp_life.q_p1: We are also preparing small personal quests. They aren’t meant to replace the main game. They are meant to add atmosphere and give participants small reasons to interact.
page.camp_life.ki_p1_pre: For younger children we are preparing a separate children’s game. It’s mainly for children roughly aged
page.camp_life.ki_p1_post: , up to about 10. Younger children can only join with a parent.
page.camp_life.ki_p2: The children’s game will run on Thursday, Friday and Saturday. On Friday it will mainly be games, workshops and activities on the meadow and in the forest. On Saturday during the main battle we’re preparing a station-based game, tasks and a treasure adventure.
page.camp_life.end_h: Come earlier. There will be play.
page.camp_life.end_p1: We believe there are plenty of new things. And we hope you’re looking forward to them as much as we are.
page.camp_life.end_p2: At the same time we know not everything has to be perfect on the first try. Camp life doesn’t happen because an organiser writes about it on the website. It happens because people start to play.
page.camp_life.end_p3: So come, take part, trade, sing, bet, negotiate, offer services, take on tasks and build Middle-earth with us. Without you it will just be a meadow. With you it can be the camp of armies before the great battle.
page.camp_life.footnote: Some details (number of coins, exact scope of the Friday game, contact person for camp RP) will be added during June based on current organisational preparation.

page.parents.intro_p1_pre: If your child has convinced you they want to come to

page.parents.intro_p1_post: , you’re in the right place. Here you’ll find an overview of what the event is, from what age children can take part, how we handle safety, what documents we need and what the child should bring.
page.parents.intro_p2_pre: The Lord of the Rings is a big weekend
page.parents.intro_p2_strong: LARP inspired by J. R. R. Tolkien’s world
page.parents.intro_p2_post: . Participants pick a side and an army, prepare a costume, weapon and character, and live a story together in the world of Middle-earth. They get camp life, programme, roleplay, costumes, community and above all the Saturday battle.
page.parents.intro_p3_post: and run by people with long experience of similar events.
page.parents.h_larp: What LARP is and what combat looks like
page.parents.larp_p1: LARP is a game played live. Participants aren’t just spectators — they enter the story themselves. They put on a costume, play a character and engage with what’s happening according to the rules.
page.parents.larp_p2_pre: Combat is part of The Lord of the Rings. We don’t fight with real weapons. We use
page.parents.larp_p2_post: , typically swords, axes, spears, shields or bows, which must pass an organiser check. The weapons are not metal and they are designed to be as safe as possible for play.
page.parents.larp_p3_pre: Even so, it’s good to expect
page.parents.larp_p3_strong: an active outdoor activity in the terrain
page.parents.larp_p3_post: . People run, fight, play outside and in the forest. A scrape, bruise, fall or sprained ankle can happen. Serious injuries at events like this aren’t common, but they can’t be entirely ruled out — same as with sports, summer camps or other outdoor activities.

page.parents.h_alone: When the child travels without parents
page.parents.alone_p1: If you’re sending an older child to the event without you, please check mainly these things:
page.parents.alone_l1: the child has a valid registration,
page.parents.alone_l3: they have a printed and signed application / legal guardian’s consent,
page.parents.alone_l4: they have a health insurance card,
page.parents.alone_l5: they have an ID or other identity document if they already have one,
page.parents.alone_l6: they know who their adult escort or supervisor is,
page.parents.alone_l7: they have any necessary medication and know when to take it,
page.parents.alone_l8: any health information is reported to the medic at registration,
page.parents.alone_l9: they have suitable equipment for the camp, the forest and the weather,
page.parents.alone_l10: they understand they must respect the organisers’ instructions.
page.parents.alone_p2: For children and younger participants it’s important they know that a simple rule applies at the event:
page.parents.alone_p3: It isn’t because we want to ruin the adventure. It’s so that the game stays safe, fair and manageable for everyone.
page.parents.h_with: When you travel with the child
page.parents.with_p1_pre: You can come with the child as a
page.parents.with_p1_post: . You can be in camp, watch from a safe distance, help the child with equipment, rest or orientation on site.
page.parents.with_p2: You can also take part more actively. You can register as a playing participant, choose a side and an army, prepare a costume and live the weekend fully alongside everyone else.
page.parents.with_p3: If you come only as escort, we still ask you to respect the atmosphere. Ideally simple, non-distracting clothing in natural colours, possibly a cloak, tunic or another basic costume element. You will help maintain the impression of Middle-earth and won’t look like a 21st-century guest in the camp.
page.parents.safety_eq_p1: We recommend that children and younger participants have basic protective equipment. It isn’t just about rules — it’s about comfort and confidence.
page.parents.safety_eq_l2: sturdy non-distracting footwear for the forest,
page.parents.safety_eq_l4: their own bottle or canteen for water,
page.parents.safety_eq_l5: for younger and smaller participants also a helmet or suitable head protection,
page.parents.safety_eq_l6: a costume the child can move in safely,
page.parents.safety_eq_l7: a weapon that passes the check.
page.parents.safety_eq_note: Don’t underestimate gloves. Unbruised fingers will thank you.
page.parents.take_l8: a signed application / legal guardian’s consent if the participant is under 18,
page.parents.take_l9: a bottle or canteen for water,
page.parents.take_l10: a snack and something quick for an energy boost,
page.parents.take_l12: a good mood and a willingness to play fair.

page.parents.h_battle: Can I go to the main battle and leave the child at the children’s game?
page.parents.battle_p1: Yes, for children of an appropriate age we plan for this. If the child can manage the programme on their own, they can take part in the children’s game while the parent goes to the main game or battle.
page.parents.battle_p2: For younger children, however, we need the parent or an arranged adult escort to be nearby and join in as needed. For children roughly aged 3 to 5, parental escort during the children’s game is required.
page.parents.battle_p3: We will be very glad if parents help directly with the children’s game too. Small things help: helping at a station, escorting a small group, handing out water, calming a young adventurer or supporting the atmosphere of the game. Every bit of help counts.

page.world_intro.meta_title: Introduction to the world of Middle-earth — Eru, Valar, Arda
page.world_intro.description: A brief introduction to the cosmology of Tolkien’s world: Eru Ilúvatar, Ainur, Valar, Maiar, Arda, Eä and the origin of evil in Melkor and Sauron.
page.world_intro.title: Introduction to the world
page.world_intro.subtitle: Before the horns sound and the armies clash, it’s worth knowing how the world even came to be.
page.world_intro.summary: The world of Middle-earth is part of a larger whole — Arda. It was created by Eru alone through the music of the Ainur. The mightiest Ainur, the Valar, watch over Arda from the distant West. The lesser Maiar serve as messengers and warriors. From one of the Ainur, Melkor, evil arose; from his servant Sauron then came the Shadow that runs through the whole known story.
page.world_intro.eru_p1_pre: At the beginning of all stands
page.world_intro.eru_p1_post: — the One, father of all. He is not lord of one nation or one place; he is the source of the music that gave the world its shape and of the fate that flows through it.
page.world_intro.eru_p2: In Tolkien’s conception Eru never intervenes in the affairs of Middle-earth directly. When evil reaches a point that requires intervention from above, he does it through the Valar, the Maiar or through fate — what sometimes looks like coincidence but never quite is.
page.world_intro.h_ainur: The Ainur and the Great Music
page.world_intro.ainur_p1_pre: Before the world Eru created the
page.world_intro.ainur_p1_mid: — spiritual beings to help him. Together they sang a great Music (
page.world_intro.ainur_p1_mid2: ), in which the future story of Arda was set out. From this music the world was then established by the word
page.world_intro.ainur_p2_pre: Some of the Ainur descended into the world to watch over it. From them came two groups:
page.world_intro.ainur_p2_mid: — the mightiest, something like gods of being — and the
page.world_intro.ainur_p2_post: , their servants, messengers, warriors. Among the Maiar are both Sauron and those who stand against him: Gandalf, Saruman, Radagast — who come to Middle-earth in the form of the Istari.
page.world_intro.arda_p1_pre: The world in which the story of The Lord of the Rings takes place is not called “Middle-earth”. Middle-earth is just
page.world_intro.arda_p1_mid2: . In the west of Arda lies
page.world_intro.arda_p1_post: , the unreachable land of the Valar. Between them is the Great Sea.
page.world_intro.arda_p2: Middle-earth itself is long. Forodwaith stretches across its north, Harad along its south; in the east lie lands beyond the sight of its known powers. The story of The Lord of the Rings takes place only in its western strip — from the Grey Havens and the Shire in the north-west to Mordor and Harad in the south-east.
page.world_intro.evil_p1_pre: Among the Ainur there was one —
page.world_intro.evil_p1_mid: — who wanted to set himself above the others. In the music he played not harmony but his own song; in Arda he then began to spoil what the Valar were creating. Unlike the beings of other mythologies, here evil does not stand on its own but is
page.world_intro.evil_p1_post: — it has no power of its own to create, it can only blight and muddy.
page.world_intro.evil_p2_pre: After long wars Melkor fell, was bound and led out of the world. But his shadow did not vanish. His first servant,
page.world_intro.evil_p2_post: , remained, and the whole later story — the entire Second and Third Age — is a continuation of this old war under another name.
page.world_intro.h_races: Peoples and the Children of Eru
page.world_intro.races_p1_pre: Eru brought two main races to Arda. First awoke the
page.world_intro.races_p1_mid: — the elves. After them came the
page.world_intro.races_p1_post: — humans. Dwarves, with their unusual origin, came from Aulë’s work and Eru’s acceptance; the Ents were then awakened by Yavanna to protect the trees.
page.world_intro.races_p2_pre: Orcs, trolls and other creatures of the Shadow are, in Tolkien’s conception, the result of
page.world_intro.races_p2_post: — Melkor cannot create them, he only twists what already exists. This logic matters for understanding their behaviour in the world.
page.world_intro.alert_p_pre: Some parts of the cosmology are more an interesting backdrop than something you need for the game. For practical event participation you don’t need to know the whole Silmarillion — it’s enough to know that the world
page.world_intro.alert_p_strong: is not created as an even game between two sides
page.world_intro.alert_p_post: , but as a reflection of the struggle between order and its corruption. The atmosphere we try to keep this year flows from that.
page.world_intro.footnote: Texts are paraphrased, without direct quotations from Tolkien’s books. Where our game conception differs from the canon, we use the marker “in our game conception”.

page.world.year_p1: The Lord of the Rings is a LARP interpretation of Tolkien’s world. We start from the atmosphere, peoples and main conflicts, but we keep the freedom for our own story and our own decisions of characters. It is not a literal transfer of the books or the film — it is a weekend in which players share a world together and create another part of its story.

page.timeline.intro: Tolkien’s chronicle of the history of Middle-earth is recorded in ages. The Second Age ended with Sauron’s fall at the gates of Mordor and the rise of the Shadow that would, in the Third Age, lead to open war. To help you orient yourself, we offer three levels of detail — pick what you need.

page.timeline.h_fourth: What changes after Sauron’s fall — the Fourth Age
page.timeline.fourth_p1_pre: After the destruction of the One Ring begins the
page.timeline.fourth_p1_post: — the age of Men. Aragorn is crowned as Elessar; the united kingdom of Gondor and Arnor is restored. Rohan and Gondor remain faithful allies.
page.timeline.fourth_p2: Sauron’s direct power falls. Orc bands in the mountains and in Mordor disintegrate — without a central lord they devour each other, vanish into the rocks or eventually attack only in smaller, fragmented raids. Harad and the Easterlings make truce and trade treaties with Gondor.
page.timeline.fourth_p3: For the elves the Fourth Age is a time of departure. The three elven rings lose their power; Galadriel, Elrond, Gildor and many others sail from the Grey Havens. Lothlórien begins slowly to fade, Rivendell loses the power of the Three. The dwarves at Erebor and the Iron Hills prosper, but Khazad-dûm remains lost.

page.practical.eq.alert_warn_body: Every participant goes through a mandatory weapon and costume safety check on arrival. Without approval you can’t play.

page.practical.food.title: Food & drink
page.practical.food.p1: As organisers we don’t directly provide catering. Each participant is responsible for their own food and drink.
page.practical.food.p2_pre: To make the stay more comfortable, we’re arranging the on-site pub
page.practical.food.p2_post: , where you’ll be able to buy food and drink from their menu and operating capacity.
page.practical.food.p3: We recommend bringing your own basic reserve of food and drink, especially if:
page.practical.food.li5: you know that without a second dinner you turn into an orc.
page.practical.food.note: Drinking water will be available on site from a delivered tank. Don’t expect showers, electricity or the comfort of the inn at Rivendell — we’re on a meadow, in nature.

faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
faq.subheading: The most common questions before the event
faq.q1: Is the event suitable for newcomers?
faq.a1: Yes — we run a programme for complete newcomers including intro workshops, rule briefings and the option to join one of the bigger groups.
faq.q2: What do I need for a costume?
faq.a2: A basic costume must match the Middle-earth theme of your chosen army. Specific requirements are in the Armies section of your side. If you don’t have a costume yet, see the Newcomers section.
faq.a3: Registration runs online via Registračka.cz. After filling in the form you’ll get confirmation and payment instructions. Payment must be made within 10 days.
faq.a4: A medic is always present at the event. Combat rules are designed to minimise injury risk. If anything happens, find the nearest organiser.
faq.q5: How much does the event cost?
faq.a5: The fee depends on the date of registration. The current price is in the Registration section.
faq.q6: Can I bring my own weapon?
faq.a6: Only LARP-safe weapons that pass the safety check. Sharp, metal or unsafely hard weapons are not allowed.
